previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: Mr. ___ , a man with secondary progressive multiple sclerosis and a history of recurrent urinary tract infections, was admitted with weakness, decreased oral intake, and lightheadedness, symptoms typical of his usual UTI presentations. He performs self-catheterization but with suboptimal hygiene practices. Initial evaluation showed no fever or leukocytosis, and a chest X-ray revealed no acute process. Urine culture grew Klebsiella pneumoniae sensitive to multiple antibiotics, including ciprofloxacin and meropenem. He was treated with IV meropenem during hospitalization, with improvement in symptoms. Blood cultures showed no growth. He received education on proper catheterization technique to reduce future infection risk. He was discharged home with services on a 14-day course of oral ciprofloxacin and instructions to restart methenamine hippurate after completing antibiotics, with follow-up arranged.

radiology_notes.text:
INDICATION:  Fever and cough.

COMPARISON:  ___.

UPRIGHT AP AND LATERAL VIEWS OF THE CHEST:  Cardiac, mediastinal and hilar
contours are normal.  The pulmonary vascularity is normal.  A 5-mm calcified
nodule projecting over the right lower lung field is unchanged, compatible
with a granuloma.  The lungs are otherwise clear without focal consolidation. 
No pleural effusion or pneumothorax is present.  Cervical spinal fusion
hardware is noted.  There is diffuse gaseous distention of the colonic loops
of bowel within the upper abdomen.

IMPRESSION:  No acute cardiopulmonary abnormality.
